refuted.title: `Subscription` drops the `state` field, so Disabled/Warned/Deleted subscriptions are fanned out to and their failures counted as coverage gaps (`skipped`) or logged as warnings
refuted.verifier_notes: The premise — 'Reads against a Disabled/Deleted subscription fail' — is contradicted by Microsoft Learn 'Azure subscription states': Disabled, Warned, Expired and Past Due subscriptions all explicitly allow GET ('Your resources are still available, so you can retrieve or delete them (GET, DELETE)'; only PUT/PATCH/POST are blocked), and Deleted subscriptions have their resources removed and are not a persistent listing state. So the fan-outs in managed_identity.rs:223-246, keyvault_rbac.rs:113-131, keyvault.rs:204-227, readiness.rs:220-250 and usage.rs:90-115 do not pay failed round trips for non-Enabled subscriptions, and `skipped`/`vaults_failed` are not inflated by them. Worse, the proposal to partition out `state != "Enabled"` would HIDE genuine role assignments and vaults on disabled subscriptions — grants that become live again on reactivation — which is a regression for a security-posture tool. Adding `state` to `Subscription` (models.rs:14-20) as display metadata would be harmless but has no coverage-accuracy benefit.

area_summaries.backend-crates/core-audit: The core audit module is in strong shape: every rule is a focused helper folded in order, scope-awareness consistently carries the resource (ResourcePermission) and gates positively, (resource, value) dedup and the redundancy planner are order-independent and well pinned, and two characterization snapshots plus ~60 rule tests cover most branches. The weak spots are risk-model consistency rather than mechanics: Rule 13 flags declared delegated scopes while its own docs and the UI group promise admin-consented ones; the risk tables apply their stated write=high / read=medium rule unevenly (Calendars.ReadWrite medium, Contacts.Read / MailboxSettings.Read / Device.Read.All zero); Rule 7 counts multi-year certificates as "long-lived secrets" while Rule 17 pushes toward certificates; and three emitted issue markers have no finding group, so org-wide reach on the legacy Office 365 resources is scored but invisible in the findings-first workbench. Several in-code docs have drifted from the code after the recent resource-aware refactors, and the legacy PowerShell citations the module rests on are unverifiable from the repo.
area_summaries.backend-crates/core-infra-a: The core-infra slice is in strong shape where the repo has clearly invested: the LRU+TTL cache's store-after-invalidate guard (IndexWatch refcounting, hold-across-store, stamp-based rollback) is correct and exhaustively tested; the four-bucket lock split, the {tenant}| key convention, the sign-out sweep across every CacheKind, and the typed-accessor "wrong door misses, never evicts" rule all hold; retry budget, Retry-After honouring, RetryClass and the http_error_enum! taxonomy are single-sourced and pinned by conformance tests; TokenError codes survive every client's BearerProvider boundary. The weak spots are around the edges the invariants do not reach: the documented auto-update opt-out (settings.auto_update / AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE) is never read by anything, the Exchange transport still open-codes its retry loop and so replays New-* cmdlets after transient failures (the exact hazard RetryClass was introduced for, invisible to the trust.rs invariant), UserSettings::mutate will overwrite an unparseable settings.json with defaults, and private_file's predictable, symlink-following temp path is used for operator-chosen export locations. Several docs-in-code comments have drifted from the code (per-object cap coverage, "four unified clients", writer count in AGENTS.md).
area_summaries.backend-crates/core-infra-b: The core-infra-b slice is in good shape where it has been fought over: the scoping gates (resource-aware Exchange/SharePoint predicates, Selected-scope levels, `selected_scope_accepts`) are exhaustively tested and match Microsoft's model, the federation and redirect validators close real userinfo-host tricks, and every Entra/Azure role GUID in the capabilities catalog and azure_roles is correct. The weak spots are places where Microsoft moved after the code was written: the FIC model cannot deserialize a flexible federated credential (null `subject`), the mailbox advisory's name-shaped fallback misses the `MailboxItem.*` / `MailboxFolder.*` / `Mail-Advanced.*` application permissions that Exchange RBAC now scopes, the restore's identifier-URI rewrite handles only one of Microsoft's two "default" URI forms, and the sovereign-cloud selector is runtime-env only while the client/tenant ids are bakeable. A handful of consistency items (seven `Vec` fields without the file's own `null_to_default` rule, commercial-host scope strings in the catalog, a CSP allowlist the webview never uses, duplicated GUID literals) round it out.
area_summaries.backend-crates/auth: The auth slice is in good shape where it has clearly been burned before: keyring chunking with a count marker and fail-closed load, meticulous AADSTS redaction in logs, PKCE + CSRF state + OIDC nonce binding, tid/oid re-binding after every interactive flow, and a launch restore that refuses a remembered account from another tenant. Weak spots are consistency rather than intent: the documented "CAE-ness must match the adapter" rule is broken by every interactive flow (sign_in, consent, reauth, refresh, restore) because CAE-ness is not in the cache key; `interaction_required`/`login_required` are treated as a dead refresh token and purge the whole session; sign-out tears down the in-memory session before the fallible keyring delete so a failure leaves a half-signed-out state the next launch revives; and a domain-form tenant id that the config screen explicitly accepts can never pass `sign_in`'s tid check. The interactive flow is untestable end to end (hard-wired browser open), the token endpoint has no retry, and several docs/comments still describe the pre-`TokenError` "BearerProvider flattens to String" world.
area_summaries.backend-crates/graph: The graph crate's transport is in good shape: one retrying core with verb-derived RetryClass, body serialized once, CAE single re-mint, same-origin guard on every nextLink follow, inner-429 re-batching under the shared RetryBudget, and tenant-prefixed self-invalidating caches — all heavily documented and mostly pinned by wiremock tests. The weak spots are at the seams: `list_all_sites` is the one capped tenant-wide scan that drops its truncation flag (so a >5000-site tenant's sweep is cached as complete), the grant read-through cache sits on the per-SP `appRoleAssignments` read while the tenant-wide `appRoleAssignedTo` read it describes stays uncached, the SharePoint resolver collapses 403/429/401 into "did not resolve", and the advanced-query flag is inconsistent between page 1 and continuations. Several of the most recently fixed transport behaviours (non-idempotent POST not replayed, scoped bearer on batch page 2, CAE once-only guard) have no regression test.
area_summaries.backend-crates/exchange: The pure-decision half of the crate (targets.rs, verdict.rs, aap.rs, references.rs) is in excellent shape: fail-closed by construction, every past regression pinned by a named test, and the OPATH MemberOfGroup parser handles escaping, lookalike properties, blank operands and non-ASCII correctly. The weak half is the transport and error plumbing: send_core open-codes the retry loop against core::http_retry primitives instead of with_retries, so it never adopted RetryClass and still replays New-/Remove- cmdlets after a 5xx or connection reset (the exact defect commit 8fb1ac7 fixed for Graph/ARM/Key Vault), mid-pagination errors are flattened to Protocol (losing re-auth-fatal classification), and ExchangeError sits outside core::http_error_enum! despite AGENTS.md saying the taxonomy comes from it. A few consistency gaps remain between the crate's case-folded post-write proof and unfolded DN comparisons in its callers, two list-all reads feeding the irreversible group-delete gate use invoke_optional, and docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md still names value-only functions that a repo invariant pins as deleted.
area_summaries.backend-crates/small-crates: The three small crates are tidy and well-tested at the transport level: the shared `http_error_enum!`/`http_retry` policy is applied consistently, origin guards on `nextLink` and `role_definition_id` are in place, secret material has redacted `Debug` and a zeroizing write request, and both leaf crates carry conformance tests pinning retryability and re-auth passthrough. The weaknesses are semantic rather than mechanical: the ARM client documents `atScope()` as "direct only" when Azure defines it as "at or above" (so the Key Vault reverse lookup labels inherited subscription Owners as direct vault grants), the Log Analytics client silently accepts a `PartialError` 200 as a complete result, and Key Vault `set_secret` (a versioning PUT) is classed idempotent and replayed after 5xx despite the crate's own comment naming exactly that hazard. The permissions crate is a 6-entry resource directory that still carries a full permission-catalog type surface, an always-miss `lookup_permission`, and docs (AGENTS.md, README, rules) that describe a catalog that no longer exists; ARM and Key Vault also keep two byte-identical ~90-line transport loops that the macro-generated error enums make easy to unify in core.
area_summaries.backend-crates/toolchain-runner: Toolchain health is strong: all 591 library-crate tests and all 200 web-rs host tests pass (0 failures; 2 deliberately `ignore`d doctests), default-level clippy is clean on the libraries, the wasm `cargo check --all-targets --features test-support` is clean, all 10 packages share rust-version 1.98 / edition 2024 via `workspace = true`, and every member carries `[lints] workspace = true` (web-rs restates it and `repo_invariants/release.rs:24-40` pins the two blocks together). Duplicate majors are all explained and none is unifiable by a local bump: root = RustCrypto 0.10 stack (p12-keystore 0.2.1, the documented hold) vs 0.11 stack (secret-service 5.2.0 via zbus-secret-service-keyring-store 1.0.1), rand 0.8/rand_core 0.6/getrandom 0.2 (oauth2 5.0.0 + ring 0.17), and the GTK3/Tauri upstream set (bitflags 1, thiserror 1, syn 1, toml_edit 0.19/0.20, proc-macro-crate 1/2, indexmap 1 + hashbrown 0.12 via schemars 0.8, miniz_oxide 0.8 via png 0.17); web = base64 0.22 (leptos_server/server_fn, documented in web-rs Cargo.toml), reactive_stores 0.2.5 + dashmap 6 + hashbrown 0.14 (thaw_utils 0.2.0-beta, and thaw 0.5.0-beta is the latest release), convert_case 0.6/0.8/0.11 (leptos_config/reactive_stores_macro/leptos_macro), thiserror 1 (gloo-net 0.6 via server_fn). The weak spots are gates that don't exist rather than gates that fail: there is no unused-dependency check (six confirmed unused deps across five manifests), CI runs only clippy's default lint set (a pedantic pass finds 99 redundant clones in the wasm bundle and one blocking keyring call on the tokio worker), and graph/exchange lack the error-conformance pins that arm/keyvault have.
area_summaries.backend-app/cmd-apps: The cmd-apps slice is in good shape where the repo's documented contracts are pinned by tests: tenant-scoped keys, the tiered invalidation (`invalidate_app_lists` / `_credentials` / `_details` / `_detail_state`), generation watches on the pinned indexes, the full-collection PATCH contract for `appRoles` / `oauth2PermissionScopes` (live re-read, disable-then-remove, raw-JSON round-trip), and the client-secret window (default 180, cap 730) are all implemented as documented and unit-tested. The weak spots are the paths those pins do not reach: three shared cores (`create_application_core`, both grant cores) return `Err` after a real Graph write so the command layer skips invalidation (retry of a "failed" create makes a duplicate app); `get_application_detail` caches a degraded permission resolution that shows granted permissions as not granted for the 60-minute TTL; `global_search` answers from the corpus without proving the session and the invariant that should catch it only scans command bodies and treats `graph_for(` as proof; `list_app_role_resources` has no invalidation although `app_roles.rs` mutates exactly what it lists; and `list_credential_expirations` stores a tenant-wide scan unguarded, the race the doc records as fixed elsewhere. Handler-level tests exist only for `add_password_core`; every other mutation's invalidation tier is review-checked.
area_summaries.backend-app/cmd-audit: The cmd-audit slice is in strong shape on its headline invariants: run_audit claims its CancelToken before the six-way prefetch, latches a dead session via its own reauth_fatal flag inside the dispatch_capped call site, counts unscored principals and unresolved resource indexes into `degraded`, and gates the CacheKind::Audit write on `run_is_cacheable` (exhaustively unit-tested). The sequential bulk driver run_bulk_seq is unit-tested for ordering, cancel-before-first-item and stop-on-reauth-fatal, and SP-only rows are pinned non-selectable by the GUI tests. Weaknesses are concentrated at the edges: the adaptive throttle re-anchors its halving window on every 429 so a sustained storm halves the cap exactly once; the readiness scope probe keeps a hardcoded CAE list that has drifted from the capabilities catalog (group_membership probed non-CAE, policy_write/sync probed but never catalogued); the redundant-permissions Fix silently drops values its Exchange veto blocks while its own doc says they land in `skipped`; score_one swallows a failed SP lookup and can then cache a Scoped verdict that was never reconciled; and several doc comments still narrate the retired `reset()` model. audit.rs at 2011 lines mixes orchestration, six prefetchers, scoring, cache and three export writers and should split.
area_summaries.backend-app/cmd-scoping: The scoping command layer is unusually well-reasoned: the grant-scoped-before-strip ordering, the fail-closed scope-repoint guards, the AAP migration's five-step plan with its three guards, and the toolkit-managed group lifecycle all match docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md, and the pure decision logic lives in azapptoolkit-exchange with solid table tests. The weak spots are consistency at the seams: the mail-scope verdict resolver hardcodes Microsoft Graph and therefore never produces a verdict for the EWS full_access_as_app scope that every upstream gate (targets_from_declared, the frontend, the audit prefetch) treats as scopable; the permission tester's SharePoint path and the mailbox reverse lookup each have a "read failed" branch that reports definitive no-access; the site sweep's 5 000-site cap is invisible to is_complete(); and the SharePoint grant/strip steps duplicate one another and the Exchange core rather than sharing helpers as AGENTS.md implies.
area_summaries.backend-app/cmd-sso-ent: The SSO/rollover core is the strongest part of this slice: `build_rollover` is a pure projection of live SP state (no phase is derived from cached or local state anywhere — `get_sso_config`, `retire`, `activate`/`revert` all re-read the SP; the board is cached but rebuilt from a live filtered scan), thumbprint comparisons all route through `core::thumbprint::canonical`, the metadata parser and the phase machine are well table-tested, and the cache-busting story is honest. The weak spots are around the edges: the claims-mapping codec mis-models Graph's transformation-sourced schema entry (it emits `TransformationID` instead of the entry's own `ID` and conflates the two on read, so any transformation policy is written wrong and an existing one is corrupted on save), `set_claims_mapping` leaks one orphan `claimsMappingPolicy` per save, the create wizard silently drops a failed claims/notification step, and the managed-identity Azure RBAC view duplicates management-group-inherited assignments once per subscription while carrying a `scanned` field that is a constant alias of `total`. Conditional Access ignores workload-identity (`clientApplications`) targeting entirely, which is the CA surface most relevant to an app-registration tool. Several commands are stringly typed (`mode`, `protocol`, reason codes) and `sso/mod.rs` at 2349 lines mixes six concerns that split cleanly.
area_summaries.backend-app/cmd-platform: The cmd-platform slice is in good shape structurally: AppState's per-tenant client memoization is one helper (`try_get_or_build`), cancellation is generation-based and well-tested, settings writes are serialized and atomic, every file the app writes goes through one owner-only choke point, the manifest carries only credential metadata, and the 186 registered commands, 186 `#[tauri::command]` fns and the frontend bindings are in exact parity (no orphans in either direction). The weak spots are (1) a documented auto-update opt-out that no code reads, (2) DR restore paths that turn a failed read into a confident "not found / not in backup" runbook line and a restore that is not idempotent while its own report tells the operator to re-run it, (3) the MI pass of the backup lacking the dead-session latch and skip-recording that passes 1-2 have, and (4) a webview trust boundary (CSP connect-src, plugin capabilities) that is wider than the frontend uses. Several doc comments have drifted from the code (pass numbering, cancel-flag "reset", settings resolution order).
area_summaries.backend-app/invariants-dto-ipc: The invariants suite is unusually strong: rules derive their subject from a source walk (`sources::commands()`), carry vacuity floors, and self-test their detectors; IPC parity is perfect today (186 commands declared = registered = bound, every binding arg struct and return type matches its command). The weak spots are (1) nothing in CI pins that parity — only an advisory, jq-dependent PostToolUse hook that always exits 0; (2) the trust rules still check at module granularity, the one place the "helper bleed" the suite was rewritten to remove survives; (3) the DTO crate has accumulated dead schema (Key Vault set-secret types for a command that no longer exists, MI Azure-RBAC backup fields never populated, `PermissionDescriptor`), a duplicated wire type outside the crate (`DirectoryIndexStatus`), and a dozen closed-set fields typed as `String` where the crate elsewhere uses enums; and (4) a copy-paste class of bug — missing `\` continuations leaving 18-space runs inside operator-facing strings — reaches the audit export text and an SSO validation error.
area_summaries.frontend/fe-core: The fe-core slice is in good shape structurally: TenantScopedUi::reset() covers every declared field and the pinning test asserts all 22 of them, the open-items working set has a single write path with tenant-keyed localStorage persistence pinned by a cross-tenant test, and the error sink (report_command_error_for → dead-session → consent → plain toast) is coherent and tested. Weak spots are at the seams between these well-designed pieces: two one-shot deep-link signals leak when the target pane is already mounted, the `/` shortcut picks the first filter input in DOM order instead of the first visible one (broken under keep-alive), the inline-error `CommandState::run` path skips the dead-session recovery the sink promises, and the toast stack neither dedupes nor protects sticky recovery toasts from the drop-oldest cap. styles.css carries ~80 lines of dead rules (an old command palette, owner list, MI scope panel, kbd chip) plus one undefined token, and frontend-workspace.md has drifted from the open-items code it describes.
area_summaries.frontend/fe-apps: The App Registrations slice is in good shape structurally: the detail pane, tabs and dialogs consistently use ConfirmDialog with subjects, `use_command`, keep-alive tabs, and the UriListEditor/DirectorySearch primitives are well-documented and unit-tested. The weak spots cluster around (a) the detail pane rebuilding every visited tab on each `on_changed`, which the credentials tab works around with deferred reloads but the permissions tab does not (its downgrade/consent outcome notes are torn down before they can be read, and consent failures never reach a toast); (b) a handful of ordering/state bugs (list Refresh races the cache invalidation, `pending_app_tab` leaks when the target is already open, identifier-URI writes replay a stale client snapshot); (c) primitive drift the docs explicitly forbid (OwnersTab/AddOwner hand-roll the directory search with the exact "No matches under an untouched box" bug, several tabs use red text instead of DetailLoadError, a value-only SharePoint gate); and (d) thin browser-test coverage for the Owners, Expose an API and Permissions tabs.
area_summaries.frontend/fe-enterprise: The enterprise/SSO slice is mature and heavily annotated: the rollover panel derives phase from live state, the SSO certificate board keeps SP ids in their own selection set (verified: `selected_sso_cert_ids` feeds only `BulkAction::StageSsoCertificate` → `bulk_stage_sso_certificates`), the claims editor's TransformationMethod list matches Microsoft's reference, and destructive flows (delete SP, remove assignment, revoke, delete role, remove owner) are consistently staged behind `ConfirmDialog`. The weak spots cluster in the SSO tab: a claims policy the backend could not read (consent-gated read) is indistinguishable from "no policy", so the editor renders empty and a Save detaches the real policy; the "Rotate and activate immediately" reveal is torn down by the `reload` bump it triggers, losing the show-once certificate; rotate/retire have no confirmation; and the tab makes the same Graph chain twice plus a third SP read. Around it are primitive-reuse gaps (hand-rolled owner search, raw `error [code]` text instead of `DetailLoadError`, a private `CopyBlock`), a truncating expiry helper that the architecture docs explicitly call out as a bug class, and the wizard's documented but still-pending UriListEditor migration plus stale reset/rationale comments.
area_summaries.frontend/fe-security: The fe-security slice is in good shape structurally: the load-bearing decisions are pure functions with unit tests (filter::matches_finding / issue_lines_for, groups::group_findings / group_remediation_kinds, row::pick / target_tab, scope_wizard::cart_mechanism, scope_badge::scope_cell_for, the eight bulk parse_* helpers), the three workbench invariants hold (filtering has exactly two homes, BulkActionBar is the only bulk caller, BulkAction::Grant is never passed on an audit surface), and the "structured signals" rule is followed for every finding key that has a structured field. The weak spots are disclosure and consistency: a truncated or degraded run with findings is shown with no caveat anywhere on screen (only the cancelled case reaches the posture strip, and the truncated/degraded text lives in the no-findings branch), the Permissions-tab AAP migration toasts success on a `partial` report that the sibling audit dialog correctly keeps inline, the wizard's SharePoint/item paths have no way back from the org-wide radio, and the documented "adding a mechanism touches exactly three places" is overstated by roughly a factor of three. The two 1200-1500-line components split cleanly along existing seams, and the same consent-callout and mailbox-group-input markup is hand-rolled in 8 and 4 places respectively.
area_summaries.frontend/fe-tools: The fe-tools slice is in good shape structurally: every surface routes through Session helpers, the Resource Access panels and DR view are unusually honest about partial coverage, and the module docs record the reasoning behind most decisions. The weak spots are (1) one operator-facing claim in the DR view that the backend does not honour (a re-run restore duplicates the estate rather than "recreating only what is missing"), (2) the shared `report_if_session_dead` recovery convention being applied in only two of the nine error surfaces here, (3) a cross-tenant residue in the Key Vault browser (listed secrets survive tenant switch), and (4) an IPC layer whose error path `unwrap()`s deserialization so any non-`UiError` rejection panics the app. Test coverage is thin for exactly the surfaces with security-relevant behaviour (Key Vault reveal wipe, DR skipped-object notice, Home dashboard, cache dialog).
area_summaries.frontend/fe-tests: The fe-tests slice is in good shape structurally: the harness (test_support + ipc_mock) is well-reasoned (orphan-mount sweep, loud-reject unmocked policy, typed fixtures serialized through the real serde-wasm-bindgen path), the 4 shards hold 130 browser tests across 32 modules (42/27/32/29) with every module I read asserting on behaviour rather than markup alone, and demo_fixture_coverage genuinely pins the one panic-class invariant. The weaknesses are coverage shape and demo honesty: 125 of the 186 command literals in src/bindings are never referenced by any GUI test, and the untested set is exactly the mutation-heavy surfaces (SSO wizard, federated credentials, Expose-an-API full-collection PATCHes, create/delete app, enterprise access/app-roles, bulk Delete, UpdateSplash); the demo's audit/credential/SSO rows carry ids that do not match its own catalog so "Open" lands on a "Demo App" placeholder, its fixed credential dates have aged past today so list badges contradict the Credentials tab, and ~13 read commands are unregistered so whole tabs show the "not available in the live demo" rejection. Harness-level debt is small but real: `click_button` is copy-pasted in 11 modules, view_smoke sits in the wrong shard and double-links the DR view, and the build_support.rs comment claiming "nothing checks" parser agreement is stale while the invariant test that does check it re-implements the parser instead of mounting it.
area_summaries.frontend/fe-a11y-ux: The frontend's a11y foundations are unusually strong for a desktop admin app: every click handler sits on a real <button> (57/57), all 13 dialogs wire use_focus_trap + use_escape + aria-labelledby, TabBar implements the full WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, the open-items workspace uses inert + focus return, colour tokens all clear WCAG AA (worst text pair is dark --text-faint on --surface-raised at 4.05:1), 34 :focus-visible rules pair with the outline:none resets, and prefers-reduced-motion is handled globally. The weaknesses are (1) the documented primitives are widely bypassed — Badge 45 bypasses vs 20 uses, ~11 raw data-tables without DataTable/keynav, ~10 load failures that skip DetailLoadError, Spinner as Suspense fallback in ~9 content regions, 8 row buttons missing the documented cell-mid — so the "one primitive per pattern" invariant is aspirational in places; (2) async outcomes are largely silent to AT (66 form-error sites, one with a role; DetailLoadError and the Copied badge have no live role) and structural ARIA is thin (0 of 87 <th> carry scope, accordion headers and FilterChips lack expanded/pressed state, two role=menu disclosures lack the menu keyboard contract, the date-range labels are not associated with their inputs); (3) two fresh instances of the documented aria-boolean-attribute bug and a hard-coded-plural / date-format sprawl (120 "(s)" strings, three expiry phrasings, six date formats) with no GUI test pinning any ARIA state value.
area_summaries.cross-cutting/tooling: The tooling layer is unusually well-reasoned: every workflow/recipe carries its rationale, the CI/verify parity, version identity, CHANGELOG format, scope allowlist and advisory-ignore lists are all pinned by tests, and the seven hooks fail open cleanly outside a checkout. The weak spots are at the seams the tests do not reach: `just setup` (the documented first command) runs `cargo check` before any frontend dist exists and so panics on a fresh clone; the CI docs-only detector classifies AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md and the commit hook as docs even though `repo_invariants/release.rs` `include_str!`s all three, so the tests that pin them are skipped exactly when they change; the Pages workflow does not redeploy on changes to web-rs's two path-dependency crates; and the release guard runs audit but not deny, so `yanked = "deny"` is unenforced on the exact lockfile that ships. A handful of comments (CodeQL 2.25.6 / a branch that no longer exists, "committed dist/ stub", the sha2 "second major" rationale) have drifted from the current tree.
area_summaries.cross-cutting/docs-drift: The documentation set is unusually rich and mostly accurate: AGENTS.md's invariants, the justfile recipes, the CI/release descriptions, the permission table, cloud/env-var/settings paths, and nearly every function/const name cited in the ten architecture docs resolve to real code. The drift is concentrated where the code moved faster than the prose: the operator-RBAC role definitions lag the service-principal-side features (SAML cert rollover, claims mapping, SP delete/owners/tags) and grant a Key Vault delete the app never calls; README's Features section and OPERATOR-ROLES.md never mention disaster-recovery backup/restore, the Vault-access reverse lookup, the Settings page or the SSO certificate board; and several module splits (`service.rs` → `service/`, `client.rs` → `client/transport.rs`, `state.rs` → `state/`) left stale paths in five docs. Two architecture-doc rationales (BearerProvider "flattens to String", "extend BOTH matches! sets") now contradict AGENTS.md and the code, and the DEVELOPMENT.md incident runbook would fail the release guard as written. AGENTS.md sits 2 bytes under its budget with at least ~1.7 KB of text duplicated verbatim elsewhere.
area_summaries.cross-cutting/security: The security posture of the user's own code is unusually strong: PKCE + state + nonce on a 127.0.0.1 loopback, tid/oid re-binding after every interactive flow, zeroized access tokens with redacted Debug on every secret-bearing type I could find except one, chunked keyring storage with torn-set detection, a single `same_origin` guard applied on every nextLink follow in all four HTTP clients, consistent `escape_odata`/`escape_opath`/verbatim-KQL escaping, CSV formula-injection and HTML escaping in exports, owner-only atomic file writes, SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege workflow tokens, and cargo-deny/audit on both lockfiles. The weak spots are at the edges: the first-run config accepts a tenant *domain* that `sign_in` then rejects unconditionally (sign-in impossible), the SSO/federation-metadata URLs hard-code the commercial login host despite a sovereign-cloud abstraction existing, the updater signing key is in the environment of the entire `cargo tauri build` (every dependency build script) rather than a post-build signing step, and the webview CSP/capabilities grant reach (14 Microsoft origins incl. a `*.vault.azure.net` wildcard, updater + dialog plugin permissions) that the WASM frontend never uses.
area_summaries.cross-cutting/deps-hygiene: Dependency hygiene is deliberate and well-argued where it matters: the crypto holds (no rsa, p12-keystore 0.2.x, transitive-only sha2) are still valid against today's registry (cms max is still 0.3.0-pre.2, p12-keystore 0.3.2 rides it), the two advisory ignore lists are in sync and pinned by a test, the RUSTSEC-2024-0429 drop condition is not met (glib locked at 0.18.5, fix needs 0.20), every license expression in both trees falls inside deny.toml's allow list, no dependency's rust_version exceeds MSRV 1.98 (web-rs max is 1.88), both lockfiles are current to within one zerocopy patch, and every duplicate major in `cargo tree -d` is transitive and platform-bound (GTK3/glib on Linux, swift-rs on macOS, schemars/system-deps at build time, oauth2's rand 0.8) with nothing unifiable from a direct bump. The weak spots are the opposite of the documented ones: six declared-but-unused dependencies (anyhow, thiserror in src-tauri; tracing in keyvault, arm and web-rs) with no tooling gate to catch them, a `[workspace.dependencies]` alias for keyring-core that names a package cargo cannot resolve, system-proxy support for every Graph/Exchange call riding on tauri-plugin-updater's default features rather than our own reqwest declaration, and a tauri-sys git pin (May 2026) that predates upstream's September 2026 workaround for a WASM function-table exhaustion crash in exactly the event-deserialization path this app's eight progress streams use.
area_summaries.cross-cutting/graph-api-currency: The API surface is in good shape: every Graph call uses v1.0 except the sign-in-activity report, which is still beta-only per Learn (no v1.0 exists), ARM authorization uses the current stable 2022-04-01, Log Analytics uses the current v1 endpoint, the RBAC-for-Applications cmdlets and the Sites.Selected/grantedToV2 bodies match the docs, and composite Exchange roles and nested-group limits are handled. The weak spots are (a) the scoping/audit role map deliberately stops at the AAP-era permission set, so newer RBAC-scopable Graph mailbox permissions (MailboxItem.*, MailboxFolder.*, Mail-Advanced.*) are invisible to the mailbox advisory and un-scopable in the wizard; (b) two on-demand tokens (group membership, claims-mapping) are minted with a single scope where Learn documents a required pair, and two on-demand features have no capabilities-catalog entry; (c) the SSO wizard hardcodes global-cloud identifiers although the code base otherwise models sovereign clouds; (d) the Exchange transport rides an undocumented gateway that the repo's comments and doc links present as the documented Admin API; and several ARM/Key Vault api-versions are behind current stable.
area_summaries.cross-cutting/product-gaps: The product surface is unusually complete for its niche: 200+ commands, a findings-first security workbench with one-click fixes, Exchange RBAC + Sites.Selected scoping, DR backup/restore, reverse lookups and a readiness checklist, all with honest coverage reporting. The two open least-privilege issues are well scoped by the owner (#109 unblocked and designed in detail, #110 correctly walkthrough-gated), and every seam they name exists in the tree. The real gaps sit one step past the current seams: Entra's 30-day soft-delete is neither surfaced nor acknowledged (the delete dialogs say "cannot be undone"), the Conditional Access tab parses only `conditions.applications` and so misses workload-identity CA policies that target the same SP as a client, the ownership rule is skipped for enterprise apps even though SP owners live in this tenant, and tenant app-management policies (the one Entra control that enforces credential lifetime) are absent while the audit hardcodes 365 days. Several header docs still describe restore/credential caching as future or uncached work that has since shipped.
area_summaries.gap-critic/gap-cancel-flag-sharing: Concurrency review of AppState's three CancelFlags (audit_cancel, sweep_cancel, dr_cancel), the single-flight gate, the ConcurrencyThrottle observer, and what the UI can actually run at once. Flag -> run kinds -> UI entry points: audit_cancel = run_audit (Security "Run audit", Home CTA) + all 11 bulk_* commands (BulkActionBar mounted in the Security All-apps pane, every expanded Findings group, App Registrations, SSO certificates dashboard, Bulk Actions page, plus the Create flow) + migrate_application_access_policies (app-detail Exchange scoping section, audit "migrate" dialog; no Cancel button of its own); sweep_cancel = sweep_site_permissions (Resource Access Sites tab AND the per-app site-access panel) + sweep_key_vault_access (Vault access tab) + find_mailbox_reachers (Mailboxes tab); dr_cancel = backup_tenant + restore_tenant (same DR view, independent busy/restoring signals). Because every top-level view is keep-alive (lib.rs:260-296) and every run gates only on its own local signal, cross-kind overlap is reachable on all three flags, and CancelFlag::cancel() stamps `current`, so with audit gen 1 / bulk gen 2 (or the reverse) any Cancel sets cancelled=2 and both `2>=1` and `2>=2` hold: every Cancel button stops every in-flight run of every kind on that flag. The docstrings that justify the sharing ("the two long-running loops never run at once", "the two never run concurrently from the UI") are false premises, not documented trade-offs. Progress channels: bulk-progress is one channel for all bulk kinds and every mounted BulkActionBar subscribes to it, so two concurrent bulk runs interleave in both rows; the sweep channels are per kind, but two site sweeps (Resource Access + per-app panel) can run at once on site-sweep-progress with no single-flight. Single-flight: all four gate keys are `{tenant_id}|...`; sign-out/clear_cache bump the watched generations so an in-flight holder's `*_if_current` refuses — no race bug there. ConcurrencyThrottle: the recovery loop exits within one 30 s tick after the last Arc drops and each FanOutMeter::attach builds its own tracker, but the per-tenant GraphClient has ONE observer slot, so concurrent fan-outs on the same tenant overwrite each other's tracker and ThrottleGuard::drop clears whichever is installed. sign_out prunes only graph/exchange client maps and cancels nothing; the dead-session latch (next bearer() failing) is the sole stop for a run that outlives sign-out.
area_summaries.gap-critic/gap-error-code-to-screen:
Slice: error code → producer → on-screen rendering, plus degraded-network behaviour across the IPC boundary.

CODE INVENTORY (producer → rendering):
- refresh_missing / not_signed_in — From<AuthError> (dto lib.rs:159-161) and token_adapter passthrough (http_error.rs:131-133) → `report_if_session_dead` toast with "Re-authenticate" action (errors.rs:54-66); only where a caller routes through it (F353/F427 already cover the gaps).
- consent_required — From<AuthError> only when pre-acquired via `ensure_*`; flattened to `token_error` inside client calls (F110) → `report_consent_required` toast + ~20 hand-rolled `e.code == "consent_required"` branches (scope_wizard, sharepoint_sites_section, usage_panel, panels.rs, …).
- cancelled — audit.rs:334, backup.rs:270 → dr.rs:81 neutral toast, audit → AuditFailure::Cancelled; sign_in hint exists but AuthError::Cancelled is never built (F113).
- forbidden — every client 403 → panels.rs:39 Callout (with consent_required); everywhere else verbatim `e.message` (Graph: raw body, F290; Exchange/KV/ARM: `{err}\n\n{hint}`).
- usage_unavailable / ca_unavailable / activity_unavailable — usage.rs:247, graph_err::premium_feature_err → Callout info/warn with the crafted message; no Retry (tab Refresh button suffices).
- throttled — client 429 after 3 honoured Retry-After waits → verbatim "throttled (429); retry after Some(N)s" / "…Nones" (Debug formatting, finding 1); no "Graph is throttling, wait" wording anywhere except the audit/DR progress notice driven by the throttle observer.
- network_error — reqwest send failure → verbatim "network: error sending request for url (…)" with the cause dropped (finding 2); retryable=true but no Retry offered by the toast sink.
- unauthorized — client 401 incl. the CAE "re-auth needed" path → verbatim "unauthorized (401)" (+ "Sign out and back in" hint for Exchange/KV/ARM), no action (finding 4).
- server_error, graph_error/arm_error/vault_error/exchange_error, deserialize_error, protocol_error, token_error, io, serde, updater, partial_failure (BulkError), and the 16 validation literals (invalid_pfx, cert_is_active, no_scope_group, invalid_redirect_uri, invalid_path, invalid_secret_window, invalid_certificate, cert_generation_failed, invalid_federated_credential, bad_request, unresolved, not_found, application_not_found, sp_not_found, cancelled, updater) → verbatim message, unbranched.
- Sign-in set (network, keyring, authorization, token_exchange, loopback, state_mismatch, url, serde, io, unknown_auth) → sign_in.rs `recovery_hint`: specific hints only for network/keyring/authorization/consent_required/token_exchange/cancelled; the rest get "Check your network and try again".

Sink shapes (grep counts): 56 `error.set(Some(e.message))`, 17 `<DetailLoadError>` (always shows Retry, ignores `retryable`), 12 `report_command_error*`, 11 `Callout{e.message}`, 13 `toast_error(...)`; `.retryable` is read at exactly one site (permissions_tab.rs:121). Special treatment exists only for: the two re-auth-fatal codes, consent_required, cancelled (dr.rs), forbidden (panels.rs), the three *_unavailable, and the sign-in set.

Degraded network: Graph is the only client with `connect_timeout(10s)`; ARM/KV/Exchange (60 s total) and Log Analytics (120 s total) retry network failures 3× under `with_retries`/the hand-rolled Exchange loop, so a SYN-blackholed host costs ≈4×60+7 s ≈ 4 min (LA ≈ 8 min) of skeleton/spinner with no cancel, then a cause-less "network: error sending request for url". Auth token endpoint: 30 s, no retry (F111). Offline at launch: `restore_session` maps a network failure to `Ok(None)`, so the operator lands on the sign-in card with no offline cue and a valid refresh token still in the keyring.

Answers: (1) table above; (2) no — Retry-After is never shown and the message leaks Rust `Option` Debug formatting; (3) `retryable` is effectively dead on the wire — the central sink cannot replay, `use_command` holds `op` as FnOnce; the flag itself is still reasonable advice after three automatic retries; (4) a mid-session `AuthError::Http` during token refresh becomes `token_error` (non-retryable, message "token: http: error sending request…") because token_adapter flattens every non-reauth code; (5) `unauthorized` is deliberately not re-auth-fatal (reauth.rs test) but the UI then renders it as text with no action even though the transport comment says "surfaces to the caller to re-auth"; (6) `.form-error`, `.alert`, `.signin-error` have `white-space: pre-wrap`, `.toast__message` does not, so hints delivered through the central toast sink collapse into one run-on paragraph; (7)-(8) see findings 6 and 7.
area_summaries.gap-critic/gap-launch-sequence-perf: Launch sequence after sign-in (from source): Root chains `get_auth_config` (local) -> `restore_session` (one token-endpoint round trip) -> `set_active_tenant`, which also runs `restore_open_items`. `AuthedShell` then mounts and, in the same tick, fires: (a) shell: `get_organization` (1 GET, uncached) and `check_for_update` (GitHub, not Graph); GlobalSearch issues no IPC until focus (`prefetch_search_corpus`) or typing; (b) OpenItemsWorkspace: one hidden detail pane per restored dock item (up to 8, F370 says unclamped), each firing `get_application_detail` / `get_enterprise_application_detail` / MI detail immediately (4-5 Graph waves each); (c) HomeDashboard, the only visited keep-alive pane, with five LocalResources: `list_applications_with_pairing` (tenant-wide: full `/applications` with `list_row_select` + its OWN full `/servicePrincipals`, no gate, F007), `list_enterprise_applications` (`indexes_cached`: SP index via single-flight + `app_name_index` = a SECOND full `/applications` with `$select=id,appId,displayName` via single-flight), `list_managed_identities` (joins the SP single-flight), `list_credential_expirations` (a THIRD full `/applications` with its own 5-field `$select`, no gate, unpinned store) and `get_cached_audit` (cache-only, sync). Readiness does NOT auto-run at sign-in (its resource lives in ReadinessView; `readiness_reload` is bumped only by the shell's refresh/reauth and the view's own Retry). Cold 5,000-app / ~6,000-SP tenant at 999/page: `/applications` 6 pages x 3 scans = 18, `/servicePrincipals` 7 pages x 2 scans = 14, `/organization` 1 => ~33 serial-paged Graph round trips, plus ~5 per parked dock item (up to ~40 more); the achievable floor with one shared app scan and F007 fixed is 14. (2) `list_row_select` (8 fields) is a strict superset of the credential roll-up's select (5) and of the name index's (3); `apps_pairing` and `credential_expirations` are busted by exactly the same two tiers (`invalidate_app_lists` AND `invalidate_app_credentials` both invalidate both keys), so the roll-up can be produced by the pairing scan; the name index (lists tier only) can be seeded from the same scan with its own per-key watch, exactly as the SP index already is. The caching doc's invariant "exactly two cached tenant-wide directory enumerations, and no surface may run its own" is violated by two launch-path commands. (3) Yes: Home receives the full `AuditRunResult` (up to 10k `AuditItem`s, 21 fields incl. five Vecs) over IPC to compute `posture_counts`/`ranked_actionable_findings`, the audit controller pulls a second copy into `result: RwSignal<Option<AuditRunResult>>`, both re-pull on `audit_reload`, and the backend deserializes the run from the untyped `Value` on every call; Home likewise pulls the full apps/enterprise/MI/credential collections for ~12 numbers. (4) Nothing is needlessly serialized (config -> token -> resources is inherent); parallelism is fine except the redundant scans and the eager hidden-pane fetches; readiness and corpus prefetch stay out of the launch path. (5) `beforeBuildCommand` = `just web-build-release` = `trunk build --release --locked`; wasm gets `wasm-opt=z` + opt-level z/lto/strip, but Trunk's `minify` defaults to `Never` (verified in upstream `src/config/types/minify.rs`) and neither Trunk.toml nor the recipe sets it, so the 120,706-byte styles.css and the wasm-bindgen JS glue ship unminified; no shipped bundle size is recorded in DEVELOPMENT.md / release-updater-demo.md or gated (only debug test shards via `web-itest-size`). (6) A long session retains, per visited pane, its resource values: Home holds full copies of apps rows (~10k), enterprise rows, MI rows, credential rows and the audit run; Security holds a second audit copy plus its lists; up to 8 detail panes hold `ApplicationDetail` + visited tabs. Sign-out (`set_active_tenant(None)`) and any tenant change re-run Root's `match tenant.get()`, unmounting `AuthedShell` and disposing every keep-alive pane, so retention is steady-state duplication, not leakage.
area_summaries.gap-critic/gap-updater-install-format-pl: Packaging / updater / OS-path lens. Read commands/updater.rs, tauri.conf.json, updater-build.json, release.yml (whole file), the justfile build-* recipes, release-updater-demo.md, README Install/Updates/Opting out/Requirements/Logs, DEVELOPMENT.md packaging + updater sections, web-rs update_splash.rs / shell.rs update code / bindings + DTOs, lib.rs config_directory + tracing, core::private_file, auth::token_cache, commands/export.rs, and the vendored tauri-plugin-updater 2.12.0 (check/get_urls, Windows NSIS/MSI launch, Linux AppImage/deb/rpm, macOS bundle swap), tauri-utils platform::bundle_type and apple-native-keyring-store. Answers to the slice questions: (a) an MSI or .deb install IS offered the update — the plugin looks up `windows-x86_64-msi`/`linux-x86_64-deb` first and then falls back to the bare key release.yml populates with the NSIS/AppImage payload; on MSI the NSIS per-user installer runs beside the per-machine MSI (the duplicate install the README warns about), on .deb the whole AppImage downloads and then fails with the raw plugin error "invalid updater binary format" in the splash. The app CAN know its format: `tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type()` is binary-patched by the bundler and is what the plugin itself consults — `check_for_update` should short-circuit on Msi/Deb/Rpm. (b) The macOS store is the legacy keychain via `set_generic_password` with default ACLs; unsigned/ad-hoc bundles have no stable designated requirement, so each replaced binary triggers a keychain prompt on `restore_session`, which is swallowed to `Ok(None)` and lands on the sign-in card with no explanation. (c) Logs (debug level, 14 daily files) live under `%APPDATA%` (Roaming) alongside settings.json — LOCALAPPDATA is the norm for logs (Tauri's own app_log_dir uses it); the private_file Windows branch is a documented trade-off and acceptable under the per-user profile; export.rs does no path validation at all — the OS dialog's path goes straight to `write_owner_only`, and std handles UNC/`\\?\` paths, so no rejection problem. (d) rpm is advertised nowhere (justfile/DEVELOPMENT.md say "omitted for now"); the real Linux portability problem is the floating `ubuntu-latest` runner: a workspace binary built on this glibc-2.39 host imports `__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38` as a STRONG symbol, so the AppImage/.deb cannot start on Ubuntu 22.04 (2.35), Debian 12 (2.36) or RHEL 9 (2.34) while README/release body say "runs on most distributions". (e) DEVELOPMENT.md claims the NSIS installer "asks once about per-user vs per-machine"; the config has no nsis.installMode, so Tauri's default currentUser applies and nothing asks (README correctly says per-user, no admin). Intel-mac and MSI-not-auto-updated claims are consistent with release.yml.
area_summaries.gap-critic/gap-observability-support-log: Observability lens on what a support engineer can reconstruct from the daily-rolling log (lib.rs install_tracing: EnvFilter `info,azapptoolkit=debug,desktop=debug`, 14-day retention, panic hook). Answers to the slice questions, all from reading the code: (1) No `client-request-id` is ever sent to Graph — `send_core_url_with` builds only Authorization/ConsistencyLevel/Prefer/Content-Type headers — and no `request-id`/`client-request-id`/`Date` is ever read from a Graph, ARM or Key Vault response (only `Retry-After` and, for Graph, `WWW-Authenticate`); batch sub-response headers are parsed but only `retry-after` is consulted. The Exchange transport is the lone in-repo model (captures `request-id`/`x-ms-diagnostics`, warns on every 4xx with cmdlet+status+request_id). (2) The Graph transport itself emits exactly one log line in 784 lines (the CAE re-mint failure at info); a terminal 403/404/4xx/5xx-after-budget is never logged in the transport, `From<GraphError> for UiError` (`ui_error_from!(GraphError, no_hint)`) just maps, and the frontend sink (`report_command_error_for` → toast; `use_command.run` → `error` signal) never logs, so a failed write vanishes once it crosses IPC. 15 command files performing writes (remediation, restore, expose_api, app_roles, applications/{credentials,owners,federated,authentication}, exchange/{grants,scope_group,aap_migration}, graph_roles, defaults, config, updater) contain zero tracing calls; bulk.rs logs only join errors. (3) A 429 storm during the audit lands as N copies of `transient failure; retrying label="graph" attempt=… retry_after_secs=…` (http_retry.rs:207) — no endpoint, no status (429 vs 503 indistinguishable, `RetryReason` not logged) — plus `throttle: throttled, reducing in-flight cap` from the observer; inner `$batch` 429 re-batches log nothing. Graph 5xx: same retry line then, if budget exhausted, nothing (the error flows to a toast). (4) Token refresh failure IS well logged (auth/service/mod.rs:174 warn with aad_error, redacted description, correlation_id; :534 `refresh token rejected, purging` with tenant_id). (5) Dead session mid-fan-out: audit logs `audit stopped: session is dead` once (audit.rs:359); other fan-outs latch `SessionDead` silently. (6) A panic inside a `#[tauri::command]` future does reach the panic hook (std hooks are global; tokio's catch_unwind runs after) and lands as `backend panic` with backtrace — but per tauri 2.11.6 `respond_async_serialized_inner` the invoke promise is never settled, so the UI spins forever with no toast. (7) An IPC arg-deserialization rejection is not logged backend-side (tauri's `tracing` feature is off; enabling it would record full request/response bodies at trace, i.e. secrets — not a fix). (8) WASM panics go only to `console_error_panic_hook` → webview console; there is no frontend→backend log command, no tauri-plugin-log, and no devtools in release, so they are unrecoverable. (9) At `azapptoolkit=debug` a 10k-app audit emits ~zero lines per Graph call (no per-request logging at any level); debug output is a handful of cache hit/miss and SP-index lines. PII in the log is limited to app display names in one warn (audit.rs:1497), tenant ids in auth lines, object ids in backup lines — no request URLs/`$filter` values or UPNs are logged. (10) Startup banner logs only version + log_dir; OS/arch, cloud, configured tenant id and profile are absent. (11) The only diagnostics surface is the cache dialog (stats/TTL/clear); there is no 'Open log folder'/'Copy diagnostics' affordance and no bundle command, while README:252 falsely says a failed update check 'is logged'.
area_summaries.gap-critic/gap-desktop-inline-test-oracl:
Static test-oracle review of the ~300 inline unit tests in apps/desktop/src-tauri (sso/mod.rs 21, sso/claims.rs 8, audit.rs 19, permissions.rs 17, permission_tester.rs 15, applications/cache.rs 15, applications/credentials.rs 13, gallery.rs 11, cert.rs 11, sharepoint.rs 10, readiness.rs 10, conditional_access.rs 10, restore.rs 7, expose_api.rs 7, bulk.rs 6, remediation.rs 6, backup.rs 4, state.rs 6, lib.rs build_support seam, tests/repo_invariants/commands.rs).

Q1 (why the 20 confirmed bugs slipped past the nearest test): every bug lives in a State-bound or AppHandle-bound body while every test in these files (except credentials.rs:456-597 and backup.rs:1024-1128) exercises a pure helper one layer below. The failure modes split cleanly: (a) the test PINS the bug — claims.rs:442-443 asserts `TransformationID` present / `ID` absent, i.e. F070's wrong shape, via an encoder->decoder round trip with no Microsoft-documented fixture; (b) missing negative/failed-read case — remediation.rs passes `|_, _| false` at all six call sites so the fail-closed veto branch (F022) is dead in the suite; backup.rs:1104 hands `SessionDead::new()` to the only wiremock test and never asserts `is_dead()` (F039); exchange/tests.rs:213-219 feeds only `User.Read.All` to the resolver while tests.rs:81 proves targets include EWS (F054 — two halves tested, never joined); (c) fixture cannot model the failing input — `EntraReach` (permission_tester.rs:177-192) and `Option<Vec<String>>`/`Option<HeldSharePointGrants>` have no 'read failed' representation (F055/F056/F057); `SiteSweepResult` has no `truncated` field (F059, sharepoint.rs:1234-1241); score_one swallows the SP error into a clean `Ok(AuditItem)` so `only_a_complete_undegraded_run_is_cacheable` (audit.rs:1664) tests the guard but nothing tests the producer (F023); (d) asymmetry visible from the test table — `a_signing_certificate_lifetime_is_bounded...` (sso/mod.rs:1787) has no `resolve_secret_lifetime_days` twin because the gate does not exist (F074); managed_identity.rs tests stop at `scope_level` labels, never the per-subscription flatten (F072). F001/F004 are special: `create_application_core`, `grant_single_permission_core`, `grant_admin_consent_core` already take `&GraphClient` (permissions.rs:389, 618) so partial-write wiremock tests need no refactor — nobody wrote them. F037/F038/F071/F075/F025/F026 sit behind `State`/`AppHandle` with no `_core` seam at all.

Q2 (files with tiering/invalidation/fail-closed/latch decisions and zero handler-level tests): F010 is confirmed and extends — `AppState::for_test` appears only at credentials.rs:509/543/565. Zero `MockServer`/`for_test` in sso/mod.rs (6 `invalidate_app_lists` sites: 177, 320, 707, 746, 1662, 1728), audit.rs (latch via `classify_audit_failure` and cache guard at 445, both only pure-tested), sharepoint.rs (cache-on-complete 988-992), restore.rs (Pass 4 `session.is_dead()` at 300, `unwrap_or_default` reads at 734), bulk.rs (4 `invalidate_app_lists` sites 288/393/514/593; its 4 tokio tests drive `run_bulk_seq` with identity closures), permissions.rs, permission_tester.rs, remediation.rs, expose_api.rs, applications/mod.rs (export_tests only). backup.rs has ONE wiremock test but on `GraphClient::with_base_url` (not for_test), covering Pass 1's chunk helper only; Passes 2-3 take `&AppHandle` and cannot be constructed.

Q3 (fixtures): two handler-test client idioms with incompatible base-URL conventions (for_test appends `/v1.0`, backup.rs:1080 does not), backup's `app_json` byte-identical to the graph crate's `tests/common.rs::sample_apps_json`, three copies of the `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` clock, three `RequiredResourceAccess` builders, three `ServicePrincipal` builders, eight per-format CSV formula-injection tests re-checking `export::csv_field` (already tested at export.rs:294). Proposal: `commands/test_support.rs` following graph's `client/tests/common.rs` and the existing `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn csv_columns` precedent.

Q4 (implementation-detail pins): no HashMap-order pins found (all map outputs are compared via `.get()` or iterate Vecs). Prose-matching is forced by untyped errors in conditional_access.rs (two causes, one code `ca_unavailable`), credentials.rs (`Result<_, String>` -> one code `invalid_secret_window`), cert.rs (`Result<_, String>`); markup pins in audit.rs:1960/1976 and sso/mod.rs:2248 are minor.

Q5 (seams): the `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "../build_support.rs"]` mount is the right tool for pure code that must also compile into build.rs and nothing else in the crate has that need. progress.rs's generic `R: tauri::Runtime` buys nothing without `tauri/test` (Cargo.toml:31 `features = []`; no `#[cfg(feature` anywhere under src/ or tests/, so NO test is silently excluded). The proven seam is bulk.rs:46-54 `ProgressSink` (4 driver tests via `Recorder`), but it is private to bulk and re-invented as `report: &(dyn Fn(usize) + Sync)` in backup.rs:364; lifting it into progress.rs is what unblocks handler tests for audit/backup/restore/sharepoint/tester/keyvault_rbac.

New non-test defect found while tracing invalidation tiers: set_saml_urls, set_oidc_redirect_uris and set_claims_mapping bust both tenant-wide indexes via `invalidate_app_lists` for detail-only writes (the F026 pattern, in sso).
